reachable: Yes, on both counts, and I checked by execution rather than by reading. (1) GRADIENT: I built the real arch (r22_prefix_content_xattention), wrapped it with the head, collated a real 64-sequence batch from data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd/emb-seq-train.pt in the pinned standardization frame, forwarded, and backpropagated the aux alone. `AUX-ONLY grads: xq 0.3198  xk 0.3335  x_out.w None  x_gate.w None`; 76 of 107 parameters receive aux gradient, including cmd_proj, obs_proj and every transformer layer — exactly the routing the hypothesis states. The mining rule genuinely fires on the real frame at the pinned dup_eps=1e-4 (172-192 supervised reads per 64-sequence batch, 2.87/trajectory over 256 trajectories, 87.8% of them cups_test/cvar_test), and fires zero times on independent random embeddings, so the aux is neither dead nor degenerate. (2) TRAINED-PATH REACHABILITY OF THE SCORED PREDICTION: the arch injects the cross-attention readout at pred[:, 0::2], i.e. command positions, which is where cups_probe reads (rpos = 2*r). After only 150 real training steps the zero-init readout is open: `||x_out|| 4.455, mean gate 0.400, mean ||contrib|| at cmd pos 11.50 vs mean ||pred|| at cmd pos 50.67` — the channel already carries ~23% of the prediction magnitude, so the hypothesis's third stated risk ("if the main loss never opens the gate") does not materialize. And the aux measurably moves the thing it claims to move: over the 190 mined rows in that batch, `mean attn mass on POS 0.392, on RING 0.296, argmax-in-POS 0.437` against a uniform baseline of ~1/17 = 0.06 over the ~17 allowed prefix keys. I also confirmed the head reads the SAME quantity the arch uses: `max|head_score - arch_score| = 4.77e-07`, `DEN subset of arch-allowed? True` (DEN size mean 17.03 vs arch-allowed 17.09), `ring subset of DEN\\POS? True`. No leakage path: the query is xq(h_cmd[j]) which is causal and never sees obs_j; obs_j is used only to build the loss target, and the head is train-only — all eval forwards (cups_probe._fwd_pred, M.flatten_predictions, stream.leakage_ok) are under @torch.no_grad and the hook returns immediately when grad is disabled.
summary: The code does what the hypothesis says it does. Every mechanical claim I could execute came back true: the mining rule is exactly "obs numerically equal to a strictly earlier obs whose command text differs" plus the two stated filters (head file:130-156); POS/DEN/ring are exactly as specified and I verified ring ⊆ DEN\POS and DEN ⊆ the arch's own allowed prefix; the recomputed attention row matches the arch's own row to 4.8e-7; the head adds no parameters (107 before and after wrap), registers one forward hook, never re-points forward, and returns a hard 0.0 on a no-grad forward, on a stale/mismatched tok tensor, and on the r18 arch ("head disabled on r18 arch? True aux -> 0.0"); xq/xk are (64,176) and both route to Muon ("params routed to Muon: [... 'xq.weight', 'xk.weight']" via the sibling-shape rule at evolve/chunks/optim/r18_spectral_capped_transition_readout.py:157-166); main-loss gradient to xq/xk is exactly 0.0 at init because x_out is zero-init; main loss is ~7.5 at init against align_w=0.3 ("order 5" is right); the genome inherits objective/optim/batcher from the parent verbatim and takes the partner's arch, as claimed. Most impressively, the author's headline empirical claim — validated in the jail against the WRONG renderer — reproduces on the real pinned frame: 2.87 fires per trajectory (claimed 2.92) at 87.8% routed-read precision (claimed 87.1%). The divergences are all in framing/justification rather than mechanism: the stated verification render is not the lane's render (which makes the max_class filter inert on top of the modal filter), "this aux is the only gradient those projections get early" is contradicted by the head's own 300-step ramp (aux is 13-22% of the main-loss gradient on xq over steps 2-10), "reachable only through the intervening move commands" is wrong for 27% of mined rows where the positive is also the name-nearest earlier command, and the mined depth distribution is shallower than the scored slice. None of these change what gets trained; they change what a later reader would believe about why it works.

divergences.claim: "Checked against evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl (24 real trajectories, rendered exactly as realenv.seq_worldmodel.render_obs / render_cmd render them ...)" and "A command with no stdout renders to \"cwd=<cwd> exit=<code>\\n\", which is IDENTICAL across every mv and every redirect in a trajectory ... Filter 1 drops any observation whose within-row exact duplicate class exceeds max_class (6) — this catches those, including the per-row variants with a different cwd."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The lane's eye is enc_e5_ft_nocwd_hf, which renders observations as `passage: exit=<code>\n<out>` with NO cwd (evolve/chunks/perception/enc_e5_base_nocwd.py:9). realenv.render_obs (the cwd-IN renderer the author validated against) is not the renderer any scored embedding comes from. Consequence: there are no "per-row variants with a different cwd", the whole constant class collapses into ONE class across the entire batch, and filter 1 (max_class) is inert on top of filter 2 (modal) on real data. The code still implements both filters exactly as described; only the stated evidence basis and filter-1 rationale are wrong. I re-ran the author's measurement on the real cwd-OUT embeddings and the headline numbers survive.
divergences.evidence: evolve/chunks/perception/enc_e5_base_nocwd.py:9 vs realenv/seq_worldmodel.py:32-38. Executed on data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd/emb-seq-train.pt (real pinned frame, standardize_stats+apply_stats, baseline_interleave.collate, B=64,n=32): `both filters eligible=192 positives=193 / no class cap eligible=192 positives=193 / no modal eligible=206 positives=233 / neither eligible=733 positives=2953`; `within-row dup-class size >6 fraction of valid positions: 0.314 / modal-suppressed fraction: 0.323 / union suppressed fraction: 0.323` (union == modal, i.e. filter 1 adds nothing). Reproduction of the claimed stats on the real frame over 256 trajectories: `total eligible reads: 735 over 256 trajectories = 2.871 per traj` (claim 70/24 = 2.92) and `routed-read precision: 645/735 = 0.878` (claim 61/70 = 0.871), READ-side roles `cvar_test 389, cups_test 256, read 85, cvar_expose 5`.

divergences.claim: "the addressing is trained by nothing until the readout grows. This aux is the only gradient those projections get early"
divergences.what_the_code_does: True at literally step 1 only. The head's own 300-step smoothstep ramp (head__r23_routed_content_alignment.py:189, ramp_steps=300) holds the aux at ~1e-4 of its weight through the first tens of steps, while x_out becomes non-zero after the first optimizer step and the main loss then dominates the gradient into xq/xk. Over steps 2-10 the aux is 13-22% of the main-loss gradient on xq, not the only one.
divergences.evidence: Executed 150 real training steps (real data, real objective/optim/batcher), separating the two backward passes: `step 1 ramp=0.0000 main=7.826 aux=0.0000 | grad xq: main=0.000e+00 aux=1.172e-05`; `step 2 ... main=2.141e-04 aux=4.707e-05 aux/main=0.22 | ||x_out||=0.0024`; `step 5 aux/main=0.14`; `step 10 aux/main=0.13`; `step 25 aux/main=0.45`; `step 50 aux/main=0.62`; `step 150 aux/main=0.64`. The zero-at-init half of the claim IS exactly true: separate check on a fresh net, `MAIN-ONLY at init: xq grad 0.0  xk grad 0.0  x_out grad 0.0378  x_gate grad 0.0`.

divergences.claim: "it rewards mass on the prefix observation reachable only through the intervening move commands (the query is built from the hidden state of the read command, which can only know that content by having propagated the move chain)"
divergences.what_the_code_does: Overstated. In 27.3% of mined rows the positive is ALSO the command-cosine argmax among all earlier valid positions, so a pure name-similarity addressing satisfies the aux on those rows without propagating any move chain. The narrower claim made in the mining section — "Prefix positions holding the same content under the SAME command text are in neither POS nor DEN" — is exactly true in the code (positives require ~same_cmd; negatives require ~same_content), and the ring does select the name-confusable stale answer as claimed.
divergences.evidence: Executed over 256 real trajectories: `POS is the command-cosine ARGMAX among earlier valid positions: 201/735 = 0.273`, `POS in the command-cosine top-2: 325/735 = 0.442`, role breakdown of the argmax hits `cups_test 77, read 75, cvar_test 48`. The ring behaves exactly as the hypothesis's own example says, e.g. `[b1 j=12] READ 'cat /tmp/w/cups/usr/share/misc/magic.txt.5' / POS p=3 'cat /tmp/w/cups/var/log/syslog.log' cmdcos=0.248 rank=4 / RING p=2 'cat /tmp/w/cups/usr/share/misc/magic.txt' cmdcos=0.960 role=cups_expose`.

divergences.claim: "The move depths present in those trajectories run 1..6, i.e. the aux is supervised at the same depths the scored slice measures."
divergences.what_the_code_does: On the real training root the cups_test depth histogram is 1..7 and is dominated by depth 1-2, while the scored slice is d3 (60 windows) and d4+ (29). Nothing in the loss weights depth. The hypothesis's own failure-mode section discloses exactly this risk, so it is not hidden, but the sentence "supervised at the same depths the scored slice measures" is only partly honoured.
divergences.evidence: Executed over the first 256 trajectories of data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd/train.jsonl (meta.cups.depth): `cups_test depth hist [(1, 89), (2, 74), (3, 52), (4, 36), (5, 1), (6, 2), (7, 2)]` — 64% of routed reads are depth<=2. Scored slice per BRIEF: `n=89 (d3 60, d4+ 29)`. Also, the mined set is 60% cvar (389 cvar_test vs 256 cups_test out of 735), i.e. the copy arm rather than the move-chain arm dominates supervision.

divergences.claim: "about 10-15% wall-clock overhead per step on CPU at B=64, n=32"
divergences.what_the_code_does: Overhead is far smaller than claimed in a real training loop — the estimate is conservative, so this is a divergence in the candidate's favour and costs nothing.
divergences.evidence: Executed 150 real training steps twice (same seed, head on/off): `per-step: bare 0.814s  with head 0.817s  overhead 0.4%`.
